overview:
NY-11, based on Staten Island and part of Brooklyn, leans Republican by about ten points. Republican incumbent Nicole Malliotakis is seeking another term after clearing her primary, while Democrat Michael DeCillis runs as a first-time challenger. No public general-election polls are available for the race, and no national ratings organizations have published assessments.

The financial picture is lopsided: Malliotakis has raised about $3.3 million and holds $2.8 million on hand, while DeCillis has raised roughly $183,000. Prediction markets give the Republican about a 93 percent chance of winning. The district's partisan lean, the incumbent's cash advantage, and market pricing all point in the same direction, though the absence of polling keeps uncertainty elevated. The race is rated Likely Republican, with the challenger needing a substantial external shift to put it in play.
